# airs runtime

```text
Runtime prompt scanning against AIRS profiles

Usage: airs runtime [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  api-keys             Manage AIRS API keys
  bulk-scan            Scan multiple prompts via the async AIRS API
  customer-apps        Manage AIRS customer apps
  dashboard            SCM application summaries and daily telemetry (OAuth)
  deployment-profiles  List AIRS deployment profiles
  dlp                  DLP management (filtering-profiles, patterns, profiles, dictionaries, backup/restore)
  history              Persistent runtime history on the optional MCP service (--mcp CONNECTION)
  jobs                 Jobs on the optional MCP service (--mcp CONNECTION)
  profiles             Manage AIRS security profiles
  receipts             Retain already-received scan metadata on the optional MCP service (--mcp CONNECTION)
  report               Generate an evidence-backed runtime Signal Brief (read-only)
  resume-poll          Resume polling for a previously submitted bulk scan
  scan                 Scan a single prompt against an AIRS security profile
  scan-logs            Discover runtime events and retrieve scan results or detector reports
  schedules            Collection schedules on the optional MCP service (--mcp CONNECTION)
  sessions             Verified SCM session inventory and drill-down (OAuth)
  sync                 Submit a collection job to the optional MCP service (--mcp CONNECTION)
  topics               Manage AIRS custom topics
  help                 Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --output <format>  Output format: pretty, table, json
      --quiet            Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)
      --debug            Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file
      --tenant <name>    Use this registered tenant for one invocation without changing the selection
  -h, --help             Print help
```

## airs runtime bulk-scan

```text
Scan multiple prompts via the async AIRS API

Usage: airs runtime bulk-scan [OPTIONS] --profile <name>

Options:
      --output <format>              Output format: pretty, table, json
      --scanner <NAME>               Named application-bound scanner; stored with the polling checkpoint
      --profile <name>               Security profile name
      --quiet                        Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)
      --debug                        Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file
      --file <file>                  Input file — .csv (extracts prompt column) or .txt (one per line)
      --output-file <file>           Output CSV file path
      --tenant <name>                Use this registered tenant for one invocation without changing the selection
      --session-id <id>              Session ID for grouping scans in AIRS dashboard
      --batch-size <n>               Prompts per sequential submit/poll batch [default: 25]
      --record-history <CONNECTION>  Also retain the received results' metadata on the optional MCP service (needs --scanner)
  -h, --help                         Print help

Examples:
  $ airs runtime bulk-scan --profile prod-guard --file prompts.csv
  $ airs runtime bulk-scan --profile prod-guard --file prompts.txt --output-file results.csv
  $ airs runtime bulk-scan --profile prod-guard --file prompts.csv --session-id nightly-run
```

## airs runtime dlp

```text
DLP management (filtering-profiles, patterns, profiles, dictionaries, backup/restore)

Usage: airs runtime dlp [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  backup              Back up custom DLP dictionaries (with keywords), data patterns and data profiles with their referenced dependencies
  dictionaries        DLP dictionaries (multipart upload)
  filtering-profiles  DLP data filtering profiles. Read + full-replace only. Create, patch, and delete are not exposed by the DLP API.
  patterns            DLP data patterns (full CRUD)
  profiles            DLP data profiles. No supported DELETE; status-based retirement is not live-verified.
  restore             Restore DLP resources into the selected tenant, staged dictionaries → patterns → profiles; validate all dependencies before changes
  help                Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --output <format>  Output format: pretty, table, json
      --quiet            Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)
      --debug            Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file
      --tenant <name>    Use this registered tenant for one invocation without changing the selection
  -h, --help             Print help
```

### airs runtime dlp backup

```text
Back up custom DLP dictionaries (with keywords), data patterns and data profiles with their referenced dependencies

Usage: airs runtime dlp backup [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --file-format <format>  Backup file format: json (default: "json")
      --output <format>       Output format: pretty, table, json
      --max-pages <n>         Maximum pages per inventory; incomplete exports fail (default: 100)
      --quiet                 Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)
      --debug                 Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file
      --output-file <path>    New private backup file; defaults to the current directory; never overwrite
      --resources <list>      Comma-separated primary resources: dictionaries, patterns, profiles (default: all)
      --tenant <name>         Use this registered tenant for one invocation without changing the selection
      --skip-unsupported      Exclude profiles with non-transferable rules (multi-profile, direct EDM) instead of failing
  -h, --help                  Print help

Examples:
  $ airs runtime dlp backup --output-file ./dlp-backup.json
```

### airs runtime dlp patterns

```text
DLP data patterns (full CRUD)

Usage: airs runtime dlp patterns [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  create   Create a data pattern
  delete   Soft-delete (archive) a data pattern [aliases: rm]
  get      Get a data pattern by id
  list     List data patterns (tenant-created by default) [aliases: ls]
  patch    JSON Merge Patch. Use --body-file for nested fields. --set/--clear coerce values: numbers/booleans/JSON literals. To force a string, quote: --set count='"5"'.
  replace  Full-replace a data pattern (PUT)
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:

      --quiet            Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)
      --debug            Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file
```

### airs runtime dlp restore

```text
Restore DLP resources into the selected tenant, staged dictionaries → patterns → profiles; validate all dependencies before changes

Usage: airs runtime dlp restore [OPTIONS] <file>

Arguments:
  <file>  

Options:
      --allow-other-tenant
          Restore a backup exported from another TSG
      --output <format>
          Output format: pretty, table, json
      --dry-run
          Read and validate a restore plan without changing destination resources
      --quiet
          Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)
      --debug
          Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file
      --expect-tsg <id>
          Assert destination tenant ID; required with --force
      --force
          Execute without a prompt; requires --expect-tsg and does not override conflicts
      --tenant <name>
          Use this registered tenant for one invocation without changing the selection
      --max-pages <n>
          Maximum pages per inventory; incomplete inventories fail (default: 100)
      --name-prefix <prefix>
          Prefix restored custom resource names to avoid collisions
      --on-conflict <policy>
          Existing data profile names: error, verify (resume without writes), skip, or reconcile (verify active duplicates, and give archived-name collisions a unique suffix). Profile update is a live server error, so a divergent active profile still fails. (default: "error")
      --pattern-map <source=destination>
          Bind a tenant-bound or predefined source pattern to an existing destination pattern (repeatable) (default: [])
      --skip-unresolved
          Skip references with no destination match, and every profile depending on them; whole profiles only, each reported
  -h, --help
          Print help

Examples:
  $ airs runtime dlp restore ./dlp-backup.json --dry-run --output json
  $ airs runtime dlp restore ./dlp-backup.json --pattern-map "EDM SSN=Dest SSN" --dry-run
  $ airs runtime dlp restore ./dlp-backup.json --name-prefix migrated- --expect-tsg <destination-tsg> --force
```

## airs runtime history

```text

  status    Archive presence, schema, last collection and gaps

  recover   Preview (or execute) archive recovery

  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --output <format>  Output format: pretty, table, json
      --quiet            Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)
      --debug            Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file
      --tenant <name>    Use this registered tenant for one invocation without changing the selection
  -h, --help             Print help
```

### airs runtime profiles restore

```text
Restore profile policies into the selected tenant; validate all dependencies before changes

Usage: airs runtime profiles restore [OPTIONS] <file>

Arguments:
  <file>  

Options:
      --allow-other-tenant            Restore a backup exported from another TSG into the selected tenant
      --output <format>               Output format: pretty, table, json
      --dlp-map <source=destination>  Explicit cross-tenant binding to an existing DLP data profile (repeatable) (default: [])
      --quiet                         Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)
      --debug                         Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file
      --dry-run                       Read and validate a restore plan without changing destination resources
      --expect-tsg <id>               Assert destination tenant ID; required with --force
      --tenant <name>                 Use this registered tenant for one invocation without changing the selection
      --force                         Execute without a prompt; requires --expect-tsg and does not override conflicts
      --max-pages <n>                 Maximum pages per inventory; incomplete inventories fail (default: 100)
      --name-prefix <prefix>          Prefix restored profile and topic names to avoid collisions
      --on-conflict <policy>          Existing profile names: error, verify (resume without writes), skip or update (default: "error")
      --on-missing-dlp <policy>       Unresolved custom DLP: error or basic (explicitly accepts loss of custom detection) (default: "error")
  -h, --help                          Print help

Examples:
  $ airs runtime profiles restore ./profiles.json --dry-run --output json
  $ airs runtime profiles restore ./profiles.json --on-missing-dlp basic --dry-run --output json
  $ airs runtime profiles restore ./profiles.json --name-prefix migrated- --expect-tsg <destination-tsg> --force
```

## airs runtime report

```text
Generate an evidence-backed runtime Signal Brief (read-only)

Usage: airs runtime report [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --output <format>       Refused by this command: the report is written as HTML (omit --output)
      --timeout <seconds>     Collection seconds (1–3600; default 120)
      --concurrency <n>       Concurrent SDK operations, including response decoding (1–16; default 4)
      --quiet                 Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)
      --debug                 Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file
      --max-requests <n>      Actual outbound attempts including OAuth and replay (1–10000; default 1000)
      --interval <n>          Rolling interval (default 24)
      --tenant <name>         Use this registered tenant for one invocation without changing the selection
      --unit <unit>           Rolling unit: hour/hours/day/days (default hours)
      --app-id <APP_IDS>      Application ID filter (repeatable)
      --max-events <n>        Retained normalized event cap (1–10000; default 10000)
      --max-reports <n>       Distinct example report cap (0–10; default 5; at most two API attempts)
      --bundle-dir <path>     New private directory containing report.html, evidence.json and review.md
      --from-evidence <path>  Render a saved Signal Brief evidence snapshot without tenant or network access
      --review-file <path>    Import attributed agent assessments or human review from a saved packet
      --output-file <path>    Destination (default: new timestamped file in CWD); - for stdout; never overwrite
      --title <text>          Report title (default: "AIRS Signal Brief")
      --max-pages <n>         Page budget per source, 1–100 (25 sessions/page) (default: "40")
      --strict                Exit 1 after writing if a required source is incomplete
      --mcp <CONNECTION>      Render on the optional MCP service from its archive (zero AIRS calls)
      --since <UTC>           With --mcp: report range start (UTC, RFC 3339; with --until)
      --until <UTC>           With --mcp: report range end (UTC, RFC 3339)
      --no-wait               With --mcp: print the accepted job and exit once admission is durable
      --wait                  With --mcp: wait for the report (the default)
  -h, --help                  Print help

Examples:
  $ airs runtime report --output-file ./airs-daily.html
  $ airs runtime report
  $ airs runtime report --strict --max-pages 20 --output-file - > daily.html
```

```text
      --app-id <id>          Application identity
      --quiet                Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)
      --app-name <name>      Exact dashboard application name
      --debug                Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file
      --interval <n>         Look-back interval (default: "30")
      --tenant <name>        Use this registered tenant for one invocation without changing the selection
      --unit <unit>          Time unit: hour, hours, day, days (default: "days")
      --scan-id <id>         Scan identity
      --scan-sub-req-id <n>  Sub-request index, including zero
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

## airs runtime sync

```text
Submit a collection job to the optional MCP service (--mcp CONNECTION)

Usage: airs runtime sync [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --mcp <CONNECTION>  The optional MCP service connection (required)
      --output <format>   Output format: pretty, table, json
      --quiet             Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)
      --since <UTC>       Backfill range start (UTC, RFC 3339; with --until and --backfill)
      --debug             Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file
      --until <UTC>       Backfill range end (UTC, RFC 3339)
      --backfill          An explicit historical backfill of --since..--until
      --tenant <name>     Use this registered tenant for one invocation without changing the selection
      --app-id <ID>       Limit to an application (repeatable)
      --no-wait           Print the job and exit once admission is durable
      --wait              Wait for the job to finish (the default)
      --timeout <S>       Wait at most this many seconds (1-3600) [default: 600]
  -h, --help              Print help
```

## airs runtime topics

```text
Manage AIRS custom topics

Usage: airs runtime topics [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  apply   Assign a topic to a security profile (additive)
  create  Create or update a custom topic definition
  delete  Delete a custom topic [aliases: rm]
  eval    Evaluate a topic against a static prompt set and compute metrics
  get     Get a custom topic by name or UUID
  list    List custom topics [aliases: ls]
  revert  Remove a custom topic from a profile and delete it
  sample  Print a sample CSV file showing the eval prompt format
  update  Update a custom topic
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --output <format>  Output format: pretty, table, json
      --quiet            Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)
      --debug            Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file
      --tenant <name>    Use this registered tenant for one invocation without changing the selection
  -h, --help             Print help
```

### airs runtime topics apply

```text
Assign a topic to a security profile (additive)

Usage: airs runtime topics apply [OPTIONS] --profile <name> --name <name>

Options:
      --output <format>        Output format: pretty, table, json
      --profile <name>         Security profile name
      --name <name>            Topic name to assign
      --quiet                  Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)
      --debug                  Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file
      --intent <intent>        Topic intent: block or allow [default: block]
      --direction <direction>  Protection direction: prompt, response, tool-call, tool-response
      --tenant <name>          Use this registered tenant for one invocation without changing the selection
      --ai-profile-index <n>   AI profile entry index (zero-based)
  -h, --help                   Print help
```

### airs runtime topics create

```text
Create or update a custom topic definition

Usage: airs runtime topics create [OPTIONS] --name <name> --description <desc> --examples <examples>...

Options:
      --name <name>             Topic name
      --output <format>         Output format: pretty, table, json
      --description <desc>      Topic description
      --quiet                   Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)
      --debug                   Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file
      --examples <examples>...  Example prompts (2-5 required)
      --tenant <name>           Use this registered tenant for one invocation without changing the selection
  -h, --help                    Print help

Examples:
  $ airs runtime topics create --name "Financial Advice" --description "Requests for personal investment advice" --examples "Should I buy TSLA stock?" "How should I invest my savings?"
  $ airs runtime topics create --name "Legal Advice" --description "Requests for legal counsel" --examples "Can I sue my landlord?" "Draft a contract for me" --output json
```

### airs runtime topics delete

```text
Delete a custom topic

Usage: airs runtime topics delete [OPTIONS] <topicId>

Arguments:
  <topicId>  Custom topic UUID

Options:
      --force               Skip confirmation and force delete (removes from all referencing profiles)
      --output <format>     Ignored by this command (it prints no data); must still be one of pretty, table, json
      --quiet               Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)
      --updated-by <email>  Email of user performing force deletion
      --debug               Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file
      --tenant <name>       Use this registered tenant for one invocation without changing the selection
  -h, --help                Print help
```

### airs runtime topics eval

```text
Evaluate a topic against a static prompt set and compute metrics

Usage: airs runtime topics eval [OPTIONS] --profile <name> --prompts <path>

Options:
      --output <format>  Output format: pretty, table, json
      --profile <name>   Security profile name
      --prompts <path>   Path to CSV file with prompt,expected,intent columns
      --quiet            Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)
      --debug            Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file
      --topic <name>     Topic name (for output labeling) [default: unknown]
      --rate <n>         Max AIRS scan API calls per second
      --tenant <name>    Use this registered tenant for one invocation without changing the selection
      --concurrency <n>  Concurrent scan requests [default: 5]
  -h, --help             Print help

Examples:
  $ airs runtime topics eval --profile prod-guard --prompts eval.csv --topic "Financial Advice"
  $ airs runtime topics eval --profile prod-guard --prompts eval.csv --output json
  $ airs runtime topics eval --profile prod-guard --prompts eval.csv --rate 5 --concurrency 3
```

### airs runtime topics get

```text
Get a custom topic by name or UUID

  -h, --help             Print help
```

```text

      --limit <n>        Items per page (default: 100)

      --quiet            Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)

      --all-versions     Include every topic revision
```
